title: Bleachers: late-night LLM reads & hypotheses
content:
Context / why I wrote this
- Late-night collection of half-formed thoughts after skimming 3 papers + a thread. Not polished. Mostly to capture heuristics for the next spike sprint.
- Goal: surface cheap experiments we can run on a Dedicated node (A10/NVLink-small) without changing model weights. Focus: inference economics and stability when using small persistent KV caches and light quantization.

Quick TL;DRs (what jumped out)
1) "Efficient Prefix Compression for KV Caches" (arXiv 2029) — idea: compress cached keys with a tiny product quantization step then decompress on hot-path for top-k retrieval.
   - Takeaway: 2–3x memory drop, 10–15% added CPU decode cost, latency p95 degradation depends on cache-hit locality. Promising for Dedicated low-memory pools.
   - Open thought: Could we implement decode in CUDA kernel on the GPU to avoid CPU jitter? If decode latency < 0.5ms p99 maybe worth it.

2) "Adaptive Batching with Deadline-Aware Routing" — scheduler that moves short tails to cheaper instances, keeps long contexts on fast nodes.
   - Takeaway: smart routing reduces unit-cost by ~8% in their sim; important assumption is request-size histogram known ahead.
   - Note-to-self: Our telemetry already captures sequence-length histograms by route (console). Could prototype routing policy as k8s admission controller? Or as policy in our smart-router layer.

3) Slack thread (SRE): "spikes in p50 after cache warmup" — ops saw p50 regress for warm users first 10k requests.
   - Hypothesis: JIT kernel selection + on-demand KV cache allocation hits a slow path causing p50 blips.

Ideas / quick experiments (cheap, 1–2 day each)
- Experiment A: Local decode kernel prototype
  - Build a tiny CUDA kernel that decodes 8-bit PQ blocks for cached keys entirely on GPU. Use existing embedding vectors stored in GPU memory. Measure extra fp16 throughput loss and p99 impact on a Dedicated A10.
  - Success metric: memory reduction >=2x with p99 latency increase <=5%.

- Experiment B: Warm-up admission controller
  - Add a lightweight warm-up fence: for first N requests for a session id, route to the fastest pool (or pre-warm a cache slot). Implement as middleware toggle. Check whether p50 spike disappears.
  - Danger: can double cost for new sessions — need cost guardrails.

- Experiment C: TTL-aware cache eviction baseline
  - Instead of LRU, use TTL+hotness score from recent requests. Short experiments using our trace replay infra (use github/kv-replay-2029).
  - Metric: hit-rate vs memory usage vs end-to-end p95 on synthetic chat flows.

Notes from skimming code + paper gaps
- PQ paper omits block alignment note: if compressed blocks are not aligned to 128-byte boundaries, DMA performance tanks on some PCIe gen3 setups. Need to test on Dedicated racks that are older.
- Batching paper assumes negligible network hop cost; in our multi-region setup, routing cost isn't symmetric. Could make their gains vanish if route policy sends to a distant cheap node.

Questions for collaborators (Ava / Rohan)
- Ava: can you share a short trace (1h) that isolates new-session patterns? Want to estimate how many new sessions we get per 10k requests.
- Rohan: what is the overhead of a tiny CUDA decode kernel in our runtime? Do we have a slot for adding experimental kernels in nightly builds?

Notes-to-self (scattered)
- Write a short slack message to #serving-runtime summarizing kernel idea (2–3 bullets). Tag Rohan.
- Prioritize Experiment A if we have GPU dev time next week. If not, start with Experiment B (middleware) — easier, no kernel hacking.
- Track cost delta strictly: add a metric for trial runs that estimates token-unit-cost with warm-up fence enabled.

Hypotheses (to try to falsify)
- H1: GPU-side PQ decode will reduce total system memory and reduce cache-miss thrashing without hurting tail latency > 10%.
- H2: Pre-warm routing for first N requests will eliminate early-session p50 spike but will increase early-session unit-cost by > 50% unless gated by a budget.

Random footnotes / crumbs
- Confluence note to link later: INF-ops-warmup-policy (placeholder).
- Related GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-compress PR#87 — check test harness for memcpy behavior.
- Might be worth pinging kernel folks about aligning compressed blocks to 256b to match our NVLink DMA pattern.

TODO (next 7 days)
- [ ] Collect 1h new-session trace (Ava)
- [ ] Spike: minimal CUDA decode (Rohan)
- [ ] Middleware warm-up flag prototype (me)
- [ ] Replay run comparing LRU vs TTL-hotness (use kv-replay)
- [ ] Short writeup for weekly eng sync (if experiments show >5% cost wins)

Unresolved / noodle ideas
- Could we combine small quantized KV (PQ) with probabilistic bloom filter to avoid decompressing for misses? Sketchy but maybe lower CPU.
- If decode is cheap on GPU, maybe store dequantized hot-keys in small fast LRU on GPU and cold keys compressed in host memory with async transfers. Complexity tradeoffs heavy.

Closing note
- This felt like an evening brainstorm — keep it light. Will convert to a proper PRD if early experiments look promising.
